text:
Sam: heads-up — customers in EU are reporting periodic 5xx/timeouts hitting hosted inference starting ~22:10 UTC. getting multiple tickets.
Raj: I see a small burst of 502/504 at the gateway around 22:11-22:18. p90 spikes, backlog picks up. attaching quick graph: <link>.
Maria: logs show proxy conn_pool exhausted and a flurry of downstream 502s. sample:
```
2026-03-17T22:11:27Z proxy ERROR conn_pool.get timeout (max_wait=500ms) -> 502
2026-03-17T22:11:27Z runtime WARN kv-cache miss spike, seq_len median 1.2x
```
Raj: interesting — kv-cache misses + long tail seq_len => more work per request, longer held conns.
Luke: any auth/billing errors correlated? support-bot: No auth or billing errors in last 30m for affected customers.
Sam: customer reported 10-20% request failures, intermittent work flow degradation. They've tried retry with idempotent backoff.
Raj: quick mitigation I rolled: expanded gateway conn_pool from 200->300 for eu-west for 30m, and temporarily increased upstream concurrency slot to reduce queueing.
Maria: restarted sidecar on 3 hosts where conn_pool error density highest. watching.
ops-bot: autoscaler triggered +2 nodes due to CPU/queue; still smoothing.
Sam: good. can we reproduce locally? sharing a curl that mimics the customer (short prompt, high RPS):
```
for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"rwl-13b","input":"short prompt"}' &
done
```
Raj: repro on staging with sequence length multiplier + client parallelism shows conn_pool saturation. will create a minimal repro playbook.
Maria: root cause hypothesis: small prompt sizes led to more per-second requests, caching not warming due to cold clients (low prefix reuse) -> more KV misses -> longer runtime latency -> connections held longer -> gateway conn_pool exhaustion -> 502/504 cascade.
Luke: agree. also noticed one proxy release last week reduced default conn_pool timeout from 1s -> 500ms; smaller headroom.
Sam: timeline summary: 22:10 burst of requests from a few tenants + cold KV caches -> runtime latency bump -> gateway conn_pool hit -> 502/504 spike -> customer complaints.
Raj: immediate mitigations performed: 1) bump conn_pool cap (eu-west) 2) restart busiest sidecars 3) temporary autoscaler policy loosened 4) applied a short-term routing rule to divert low-priority tenants to dedicated overflow.
Maria: monitoring now shows error rate back to ~1% from 12%. p95 latency improving.
support-bot: sent templated interim comms to affected customers: "we're investigating intermittent 5xxs; ongoing mitigations applied; follow-up later."
Sam: action items:
- Raj: write reproducible script + staging job for this pattern (due: today EOD)
- Maria: add a probe to detect rapid kv-cache miss spike and alert before conn_pool saturation (due: 48h)
- Luke: revert conn_pool timeout change or add circuit smoothing (investigate config, due: next week)
- Engineering: add a routing policy to automatically throttle low-value tenants during short surges (design doc next sprint)
- Support: follow-up customer note with timeline + ETA for fixes (Sam)
Raj: opened issue ENG-4258 with repro and initial telemetry dump. link: <link-to-issue>.
Maria: small follow-up: we should add an operational checklist in runbook: if kv-cache miss rate > X for 5m, then preemptively up-concurrent slots and warm caches.
Luke: agree. I can draft runbook snippet and share.
Sam: quick comms plan: Sam to send update to affected customer list in 2h, include ops actions and ETA.
support-bot: scheduled reminder for Sam in 2h.
Raj: monitoring note — adding a synthetic probe that emits small prompt traffic with consistent prefixes to keep caches warm might help. low-cost periodic warmers per region.
Maria: we should also review model variants: smaller models with faster latency for small prompt workloads as an automatic fallback.
Sam: final: good containment. will keep this thread as the incident debrief. please update ENG-4258 and the runbook items when you complete tasks. :thumbsup:
Luke: ack. logging action items in sprint board.
Raj: closing active mitigation 22:34 UTC, continuing monitoring.
ops-bot: Incident metrics: peak 5xx rate 14% at 22:12, reduced to 1.2% after mitigations by 22:29.
Sam: thanks everyone. follow-ups tomorrow for longer-term hardening.
